data.title: July core CPI to offer Fed more wait-and-see space: Pantheon Macro
data.description:
Pantheon Macroeconomics economists Samuel Tombs and Oliver Allen project a reassuring July CPI print that should keep the Federal Reserve from tightening policy.

The firm is forecasting a 0.07% M/M rise in the headline Consumer Price Index and a 0.17% M/M increase in the core index—modest enough to keep most Federal Open Market Committee members content with their current wait-and-see stance.

While Chair Warsh has downplayed the significance of any single month's data, other committee members remain highly sensitive to inflation readings, Pantheon Macro pointed out in a note to clients. New York Fed President John Williams has indicated his base case for unchanged rates this year would hold if core personal consumption expenditures averages 0.20% or less monthly, while Governor Waller warned before June's data that another hot reading could prompt tightening discussions.

Upstream producer and import price pressures present a notable upside risk to core goods inflation. Producer Price Index finished goods prices have continued rising modestly while consumer goods import prices have surged, suggesting potential for a CPI bounceback.

Apple's (AAPL) decision to hike prices on most hardware products by 15% to 30% in late June will likely lift the computers and peripherals CPI by around 4%, adding about 6 basis points to the core goods reading, Pantheon Macro noted. However, retailers are benefiting from a substantial cushion: federal refunds from illegal IEEPA-based tariffs have now surpassed $100B, equivalent to 60% of all tariffs paid on those grounds.

 

Meanwhile, three services categories are expected to provide deflationary counterweights to core goods pressures. Airline fares are projected to fall 1.5% in July as jet fuel prices have moderated to just 40% above January levels, down from 80% above at April's peak, while Google search data indicates flight inquiries have declined from spring highs, limiting carrier pricing power.

Accommodation prices are forecast to drop another 1% as the World Cup booking surge continues to fade from the CPI sample. Auto insurance premiums should extend their recent declines—a trend Pantheon believes marks the start of a sustained downward move, driven by record profit margins in 2025 and intensifying competition among insurers.

 

In all, July's inflation data should be just sufficient to maintain the FOMC's holding pattern, the note said, though August's readings and the trajectory of the Middle East conflict will carry more weight for September's policy decision. The firm projects the federal funds mid-point will remain at 3.625% through year-end 2026, with rate cuts starting in early 2027 and reaching 2.875% by June of that year.

data.title: Medical Properties Trust Q2 earnings on deck: What to expect
data.description:
When Medical Properties Trust (MPT) reports second quarter earnings on Monday, Wall Street expects the medical facility REIT to post FFO of $0.15 on revenue of $253.28M for the quarter.

The Trust reported mixed earnings in the first quarter, as its normalized FFO per share came in at $0.14, compared to the Visible Alpha consensus of $0.15, while its revenue of $252.07M was $2.39M higher than consensus.

During the firm’s Q1 earnings call, CEO Edward Aldag commented, “General acute performance was largely stable with EBITDARM increasing nearly $40 million year-over-year. These strong results were partially offset by our behavioral health portfolio, which continues to navigate two entirely separate challenges in the U.S. and U.K. markets. While both markets continue to experience strong demand, in the U.S., providers are grappling with staffing shortages, and in the U.K., demand is being dampened by funding pressures at the NHS.”

Seeking Alpha analysts are bullish and rate, on average, MPT a Buy.

Seeking Alpha analyst Juxtaposed Ideas rated the stock a Buy, saying that the stock benefits from the secure, inflation-beating dividend yield of 7.95% and the bullish uptrend support line established since the early 2024 bottom.

“Medical Properties Trust, Inc.'s near-term rental collections are stabilizing as new tenants ramp to full payments, aided by the stable mature tenants, with this supporting management's reiterated end-of-FY2026 targets,” the analyst added.

However, Wall Street analysts and Seeking Alpha’s Quant rating are cautious, rating MPT a Hold and Sell, respectively.

The REIT’s shares have slipped nearly 8% year-to-date, compared to the benchmark S&P 500’s 12.6% gain over the same period.

Over the last three months, EPS estimates have not seen any upward revisions, compared to one downward move, while revenue estimates have seen one upward revision and one downward revision.

data.title: Bayer granted court delay to September for Roundup settlement hearing
data.description:
A Missouri court on Thursday granted Bayer's (BAYRY) (BAYZF) request to postpone until September 14 a hearing to consider the company's proposed $7.25B class settlement of cases alleging ​that its Roundup weedkiller causes cancer.

The court had previously scheduled an August 19 hearing to consider approving the settlement, but Bayer (BAYRY) (BAYZF) ​asked for more time to review requests from plaintiffs to opt out of the settlement, and the company said some people want to ⁠rejoin the deal after a recent Supreme Court decision undercut one of ​the central legal claims in the Roundup cases.

The settlement, announced in February, aims to resolve most current and future Roundup claims in the ​U.S.; Bayer (BAYRY) (BAYZF) has said that decades of studies have shown Roundup's key ingredient, glyphosate, is safe and does not cause cancer.

The company faces ~65K claims in U.S. state and federal courts from plaintiffs who say they ​developed non-Hodgkin lymphoma and other forms of cancer after using Roundup ​at home or on the job.
